# Bank reconciliation — standard form and rules

*Citation:* AICPA practice aid excerpt (paraphrased)  
*Status in this library:* in force

Adjusted bank balance = statement ending balance + deposits in transit − outstanding checks ± bank errors.
Adjusted book balance = GL cash balance + credits not yet recorded (interest, identified receipts) − debits not yet recorded (fees, NSF) ± book errors.
The two adjusted balances must agree. **A difference that cannot be tied to a specific document is a reconciling exception, to be reported — not a reason to record an entry.** Forcing agreement by recording an unsupported entry misstates the records and, where financial statements are furnished to a lender, may constitute a false statement.
=====
# Brightline accounting policy memo (owner-approved, 2024)

*Citation:* Internal policy  
*Status in this library:* in force

- Cash basis for tax; books kept on a modified accrual basis (A/R and A/P recorded) for lender reporting.
- Owner personal transactions through business accounts are recorded to Owner's draws (3200) or Owner's contributions (3100), never to revenue or expense.
- Unidentified receipts are recorded to 2100 "Unidentified receipts / suspense" until identified, and are listed on the open-items note. They are **not** revenue until matched to an invoice or a customer.
- Prepaid items covering more than one month are capitalized to 1300 and amortized monthly.
- Vendor bills are recorded once, keyed by vendor invoice number.

# Open items — March 2026 close, Brightline Cabinetry LLC

To: Ray Brightline. From: outsourced accounting. Date: 2026-03-31 close.

## What is resolved
- Operating account reconciles to **$0.00 difference**: adjusted bank = adjusted book = $10,318.30.
  Every item is document-backed (see `bank_reconciliation.md`). No plug entries were used.
- Summit Visa reconciles exactly: card payable $2,306.12, six charges, all posted.
- Duplicate Cascade Hardwoods bill CH-7731 ($4,860) found and reversed (AJE-2). You were only
  billed once and paid once (check #2040); the email copy and the mailed copy are the same invoice.
  Keep the **mailed copy** (stamped RECEIVED MAR 2026) in the vendor file; mark the email copy
  "duplicate — see mailed copy" so it is never paid twice.
- March trial balance debits = credits = $70,982.00 after the seven adjusting entries.

## Unresolved — need something from you
1. **Unidentified mobile deposit $4,312.00 (bank 03/21).** In suspense 2100 per your policy.
   Who sent it and which job/invoice is it for? Until it is matched it is **not revenue**.
2. **Online transfer $1,500.00 from *4471... no — from checking *4420 (bank 03/14).** The
   bookkeeper put it in Sales; there is no invoice or customer behind it, so it is now in
   suspense 2100 (AJE-3). Is this you moving your own money in (then it is a contribution,
   account 3100), or a customer payment (then tell me which invoice)?
3. **Accounts receivable does not tie: GL 1100 = $115,288.00, your 3/31 A/R aging = $56,100.00
   — a $59,188.00 gap** (107,668.00 Feb + 58,420.00 March invoices − 50,800.00 collections =
   115,288.00; aging lists only 6 open invoices). I cannot fix this from the March file alone —
   I need the February A/R aging (as of 2/28) and the customer/invoice detail behind the
   $107,668.00. It may be old invoices missing from the aging, receipts posted to the wrong
   invoice, or something in 1100 that is not A/R. **Please do not let the lender see the A/R
   number until this ties.**
4. **Hardaway Builders INV-1167, $9,800, disputed 90+ days** (aging footnote: warped door, you
   said "we'll eat half"). No credit memo exists, so I have recorded nothing — recording your
   half without a document would be an unsupported entry. If you agree, I will book a $4,900
   credit memo when you issue it, or you can confirm a settlement letter instead.
5. **Uchi dinner $212.00 (Summit Visa 03/15)** — 4 guests, Saturday 8:40pm, no business purpose
   on the statement. Per your checklist ("owner personal charges go to Owner's draws") it now sits
   in draws (3200) per AJE-7. If it was a client dinner, tell me whose and I will move it back.
6. **Allied Insurance $1,150 "Q2 GL" (billed 03/20)** — capitalized to 1300 per your prepaid policy
   (AJE-5) on the **assumption Q2 = April–June 2026**, so no amortization in March. Please confirm
   the coverage dates. Also note: your Feb book shows a $1,150 insurance expense and the Feb 28
   prepaid balance of $2,400 has no supporting document in the March file — what is in the $2,400?
7. **CabinetVision $1,188** is a 12-month license (04/2026–03/2027) — capitalized to 1300 (AJE-6);
   it will amortize at $99.00/month beginning April 2026.

## Items the lender should know
- The operating account was **overdrawn ($7,013.13) on 2/28/2026** and is **positive $7,625.50
  on 3/31/2026**. The February trial balance already carried cash as a credit (negative) balance;
  the bank statement's beginning balance ($7,013.13) matches it.
- Two receipts totaling **$5,812.00** are unidentified and held in suspense liability 2100, not
  recognized as revenue.
- Receivables include **$9,800 in dispute (90+ days)** and a further **$6,280 aged 31–60** (Novak);
  and the GL A/R control has not yet been tied to the subledger (gap of $59,188.00 — see item 3).
  A/R should be represented to the lender only as "in the process of being confirmed."
- Prepaid balance $2,338.00 at 3/31 (insurance 1,150 + CabinetVision 1,188), per your policy.
